translations.translation: The philosopher speaks from rational arguments; the intellect emerges from the vestibule (of perception).

The philosopher who denies the senses is a stranger to the prophets' senses. The speech of water, the speech of the Creator, the speech of the flower is perceived by the senses of the people of the heart.
Hindus had brought an elephant into a dark house for exhibition.
People gathered in the darkness to see it; each person was in distress. Since seeing it with the eye was not possible, each one felt with his hand in that darkness.
The hand of one fell on its trunk; he said, 'This is like a water-pipe (or a snake).'
The hand of another felt its tail, which was like a broom.
He was weaving and twisting, whatever he felt. They disagreed about its form; each one spoke differently.
One gave its ear to another; he said, 'This is like a fan.' If there had been a lamp in each of their hands...
Disagreement would have vanished from their hands.
They will sit for judgment and will say that Jalal al-Din Muhammad has not wanted disputes in the struggles of life from intellect.
